query: FeCoNi is an fcc alloy with high saturation magnetization and a low coercive field. Earlier studies examined the high-entropy alloys FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt, but both exhibited soft ferromagnetism. A qualifying high-entropy alloy must have an almost equiatomic multicomponent composition and configurational entropy of at least 1.0R. Subject to these constraints, what single intervention could produce a FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy with greater coercivity than the prior derivatives? Present one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the outcome relative to an appropriate FeCoNi-based baseline, defines the conditions over which it should apply, cites supporting observations from earlier work, and proposes a discriminating experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing equiatomic Al as a fourth principal element (Fe25Co25Ni25Al25) will transform a single–phase fcc FeCoNi alloy into a dual-phase high-entropy alloy (fcc matrix + coherent B2-ordered (Fe,Co)Al nanoprecipitates).  The B2 precipitates and the associated lattice distortion will impede domain-wall motion and raise the magnetocrystalline anisotropy, giving a room-temperature coercive field at least four-times higher than that of earlier soft FeCoNiPd or FeCoNiPt derivatives processed under the same thermal history.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic Fe–Co–Ni alloy prepared by arc melting, homogenised at 1000 °C, water-quenched; single-phase fcc grains ≈20–50 µm; coercivity ≤50 Oe at 300 K (soft ferromagnet).
generation.intervention: Replace one quarter of the atomic fraction with aluminium to obtain Fe25Co25Ni25Al25, melt in identical conditions, homogenise 1000 °C/24 h, water-quench.
generation.conditions: Room-temperature magnetic measurement after the above melt–homogenise–quench route; grain size ≤20 µm; no subsequent deformation.
generation.structural_mediator: ≈5–15 nm coherent B2-ordered (Fe,Co)Al nanoprecipitates uniformly dispersed in a disordered fcc matrix, producing ~3 % local lattice strain.
generation.mechanism: 1) The B2 precipitates act as strong pinning centres that raise the critical field for domain-wall depinning.  2) Chemical ordering across the B2/fcc interfaces and the Al-induced tetragonal lattice distortion enhance the magnetocrystalline anisotropy constant K1.  Together these effects increase the intrinsic and extrinsic contributions to coercivity without severely reducing saturation magnetisation.
generation.predicted_outcome: Hc(300 K) for FeCoNiAl ≥200 Oe, i.e. ≥4× the <50 Oe measured for FeCoNiPt or FeCoNiPd processed identically; saturation magnetisation will drop by <10 %.
generation.baseline: Equiatomic FeCoNiPt (or FeCoNiPd) produced and heat-treated identically, showing single-phase fcc structure and Hc ≈40–50 Oe at 300 K.
generation.boundary: Effect persists for 10 %–40 % B2 volume fraction and precipitate sizes ≤20 nm. Coercivity gains vanish if annealed >900 °C for >2 h (precipitate coarsening) or if Al deviates by >10 at.% from equiatomic, which suppresses coherent B2 formation.
generation.uncertainty: Exact magnitude of Hc increase depends on precipitate size/stability; if B2 ordering is incomplete or grains coarsen, the gain may fall to 2× instead of 4×.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two alloys (Fe25Co25Ni25Al25 and Fe25Co25Ni25Pt25) by identical arc-melting and homogenisation.  Characterise phase constitution by XRD and TEM to confirm fcc + B2 nanostructure only in the Al-bearing sample.  Measure hysteresis loops at 300 K with a vibrating-sample magnetometer (max field ≥10 kOe) to extract coercivity.
measurements: XRD phase identification and lattice parameters
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If FeCoNiAl shows Hc ≤50 Oe or an increase <100 % relative to the Pt-bearing baseline under the same processing, the hypothesis is falsified.
